hero.title: From search export to PRISMA diagram, in one place.
hero.lede: Krinea imports your references, removes duplicates, lets two reviewers screen blind, extracts data with quotes you verify, and draws the PRISMA 2020 diagram from the counts. Open source, free to start.
hero.note: No credit card. AGPL-3.0. Hosted in Frankfurt (EU) or on your own server.

how.title: One review, five stages.
how.lede: Everything stays in one workspace, and everything exports. Every screen below is the real application, on a sample review of 55 fictitious records.

import.b1: RIS, BibTeX, PubMed, Web of Science, CSV, TSV or Excel, format detected on upload.

import.b3: The counts per source feed the PRISMA diagram from the first import.

dedup.title: Remove duplicates, keep the evidence.
dedup.b1: Identical DOIs and titles merge on their own.

screen.b3: Each decision keeps its reason, its reviewer and its time.
screen.alt: Screening view: the record list with progress, a record card with highlighted keywords and the Include, Maybe and Exclude buttons

extract.title: Extract with quotes you can check.
extract.b1: You design the form. The AI fills it from the PDF.
extract.b2: Every value comes with the sentence it was taken from.
extract.b3: Nothing counts until a person saves it as verified.

story.title: Built by a researcher who needed it.
story.p1: Krinea began as a script written during a real systematic review on long-term energy-system models in Africa. Its author needed to pull structured data out of hundreds of PDFs without losing track of where each value came from. The script grew a form, then a quote next to every value, then a screening step so the same team could decide which papers to read at all.
story.p2: Today Krinea is an independent open-source project maintained by one developer-researcher based in France, with no company behind it. The hosted edition runs in Frankfurt and is free while it is in beta. The code is AGPL-3.0, so whatever happens to the hosted edition, you can run it yourself.

two.title: Made for two people who do not always agree.
two.lede: Most reviews are screened in pairs. Krinea is built around that: two independent reads, a blind mode, a conflict list, and progress per reviewer so nobody is left behind.
two.f1: Single or double screening, chosen per review.
two.f2: Blind mode per stage: title and abstract, then full text.
two.f3: Conflicts settled with both decisions and both reasons on screen, and logged.

faq.title: Questions people ask first.
faq.more: Anything else: <contact>write to us</contact> or <discussions>open a discussion on GitHub</discussions>.

free.a: Yes. The hosted edition is free during the beta, with every feature, and self-hosting is free forever. Pro and Institution plans will open once billing and the legal documents are ready, and nothing is charged before you subscribe.

data.a: On servers in Frankfurt, Germany, in the EU, operated by Render. If you self-host, wherever you put it. The privacy policy lists exactly what is stored.

import.q: Can I import from Zotero, EndNote or Mendeley?
import.a: Export a RIS or BibTeX file from your reference manager and import it. PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus exports work directly. A direct Zotero connection does not exist yet.

conflict.q: What happens when two reviewers disagree?
conflict.a: The record is marked as a conflict. Both decisions and reasons are shown side by side, and the review owner settles it with a final decision. All the votes stay in the decision log.

ai.a: No. It suggests a decision with a reason, or fills an extraction form with a quote per field. Suggestions are stored apart from decisions, and only a person can include, exclude or verify. You bring your own API key.

selfhost.a: Yes. The repository ships a Docker Compose file and a Render blueprint. The application is AGPL-3.0 and the engine is MIT.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: A real person reads every message, in English or French. Bugs and feature requests move fastest through GitHub; institutional questions, free-access requests and anything private go by e-mail.

institutions.title: Institutions
institutions.text: Single sign-on, admin console, invoicing and a data processing agreement for universities and organisations. Tell us the number of reviewers, the review types and your data requirements.

lowIncome.title: Free Pro access
lowIncome.text: Reviewers at institutions in low-income countries get the Pro plan for free. Write from your institutional e-mail address with your name and department.

support.title: Support and bugs
support.text: The issue tracker is public: search it first, then open an issue with what you did, what you expected and what happened. Questions and ideas go to Discussions. Security vulnerabilities never go in a public issue: report them privately by e-mail or through GitHub private vulnerability reporting.

contact.response: We answer within five working days; there is no phone line or live chat.
